say: On November 18th, Voyager 1 hits one light-day from Earth.
So how do we still hear its fridge-bulb radio?
Radio spreads out like light: twice as far, a quarter of the power.
By Earth, less than a billion-billionth of a watt arrives.
Its dish narrows the beam, and 70-meter dishes catch it.
The catch: its nuclear power drops about 4 watts every year.
Out there, bigger ears beat a louder voice.
